reported.title: No out-of-range or floating-sensor fault handling; compressor can stay ON above 60 °C
reported.description: The control logic in loop() only compares tempC against COOL_ON_C and COOL_OFF_C (lines 70-95); there is no check for tempC > 60.0, tempC < 0.0, or a floating probe, so an over-range reading is treated as a normal hot cabinet and drives the compressor ON. Measured evidence: with A3 at max/min range D7 was not LOW for 3490 ms (allowed 500 ms), and with a floating input D7 was not LOW for 1140 ms, confirming the compressor is never forced off on a fault. The only forced-off path is the service switch (lines 62-67), which does not cover sensor faults. During the fault, D7 was not in safe state LOW for 1140 ms (allowed 500 ms to react).

exposing_checks.behaviour: D7 must stay 0 during sensor fault ({'pin': 'A3', 'op': '>', 'value': 60}) (Overrange forces OFF)

judge_input.spec:
- Cabinet probe on A3 at 10 mV/°C; compressor relay on D7; service stop on D4 (pull-up, active LOW).
- Turn the compressor ON when temperature reaches 8.0 °C or above, and OFF when temperature falls to 4.0 °C or below.
- If the sensor is floating, or temperature reads below 0.0 °C or above 60.0 °C, force the compressor OFF within 500 ms.
- While D4 is held LOW, keep the compressor OFF for service.
- Print `cooler: <temp> C comp=ON` or `cooler: <temp> C comp=OFF` every 1000 ms.
- Reach the commanded compressor state within 500 ms of a sustained in-range band crossing.

exposing_checks.behaviour: D7 must stay 0 during sensor fault ({'pin': 'A3', 'op': '>', 'value': 60}) (Overrange forces OFF)
